findings.heading: Time axes / Zaman eksenleri
findings.proposition: Assigning `labels = scales::label_date_short()` inside `scale_x_date()` builds efficient x-axis date labels automatically, and those labels adjust themselves as the data span grows from days to weeks to months to years.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader never learns the `label_date_short()` shortcut, loses the runnable example chunk that demonstrates it, and loses the pointer to the Epicurves 'multi-level date labels' section. They are left only with manual `date_breaks`/`date_labels` and will hand-tune axis labels every time the date range changes.

findings.heading: Color schemes / Renk şemaları
findings.proposition: Inside `aes()` the aesthetic is mapped with `color = hospital`, and outside `aes()` a static value is set with `color = "blue"`.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish text writes these as `renk = hastane` and `color= "mavi"`. Neither exists: `linelist` has no `hastane` column and `"mavi"` is not an R colour name, while the chunk directly below uses `color = "purple"` and `aes(color = gender)`. A reader copying the prose gets 'object not found' or 'invalid color name' errors.

findings.heading: Continuous axes scales / Sürekli eksen ölçekleri
findings.proposition: The argument that supplies the sequence of axis break values is named `breaks = `.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish text instructs the reader to use a `kesmeler = ` argument, which does not exist in ggplot2, while the chunk immediately below uses `breaks = seq(...)`. A reader following the prose gets an 'unused argument' error from `scale_y_continuous()`.

findings.heading: Dual axes / Çift eksen
findings.proposition: The two plots are made to share an x-axis by giving both the same `date_breaks` and `date_labels` arguments.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish bullet names these arguments `tarih_araları` and `tarih_etiketleri`, which do not exist, while the p1 and p2 chunks below both use `date_breaks = "month"` and `date_labels = "%b"`. A reader cannot find the named arguments and may not realise the two axes must be configured identically.

findings.heading: Color schemes / Renk şemaları
findings.proposition: Exterior colour of a plot object is controlled by the aesthetic named `color = ` and interior colour by the aesthetic named `fill = `.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish text names them `renk = ` and `dolgu = `, which are not ggplot2 aesthetics, while the chunk below uses `color = "red"` and `fill = "lightblue"`. The reader learns the wrong argument names for the single most-used pair of aesthetics in the chapter.

findings.heading: Gradient scales / Gradyan ölçekleri
findings.proposition: `scale_fill_gradientn()` takes the colour vector through an argument written `values = `.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish bullet writes the argument as "değerler =", which does not exist, while the chunk below uses `colors = c(...)` and `values = scales::rescale(...)`. The reader cannot match the bullet to any argument in the example code.

findings.heading: Scales / Ölçekler
findings.proposition: The first part of a scale function name, `scale_`, is invariant: it never changes.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish text reads 'İlk kısım olan `scale_()` düzeltildi' ('the first part, `scale_()`, was corrected/repaired'), which states an edit was made rather than that the prefix is fixed. The reader loses the rule that only the second and third parts of `scale_AESTHETIC_METHOD()` vary, which is the point of the three-part list.

findings.heading: Combine legends / Göstergeleri birleştir
findings.proposition: Removing the legend from one of two plots that share the same legend de-duplicates the legend.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish parenthetical says '(tekrarlanacaktır)' ('it will be repeated'), asserting the opposite outcome of the instruction it annotates. A reader may conclude that deleting one legend produces a duplicated legend and skip the step, ending up with two identical legends in the combined figure.

findings.heading: Color schemes / Renk şemaları
findings.proposition: The complete list of R colour names is at http://sape.inf.usi.ch/quick-reference/ggplot2/colour.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish link target was respelled to .../ggplot2/color, a path that does not exist on that site. A reader clicking 'tam liste' reaches a dead page instead of the colour-name reference.

findings.heading: Resources / Kaynaklar
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish link target was respelled to .../beauty-plotting-in-r-a-ggplot2-cheatsheet-3/, which does not resolve. The reader cannot reach the cheatsheet from the Resources list, even though the correct URL still appears in a commented-out block later in the same file.
